title: Unit – 2 : Session – 7 : SLO – 2 | BCD Addition
sections: 1. BCD → b. Binary representation of decimal digits
2. Correction rule → a. Add 0110 (6) if sum > 9
4. Valid BCD digit range → d. 0000 to 1001
BCD stands for BINARY CODED DECIMAL.
In BCD, each decimal digit is represented by 4 bits.
The valid range of a single BCD digit is 0000 to 1001 (0 to 9).
If a BCD addition produces a sum greater than 1001, we must ADD 0110 (6) to correct it.
The BCD sum of 0101 (5) and 0101 (5) after correction is 0001 0000 (decimal 10).
Activity – Describe and Perform BCD Addition (5 + 7)

Steps: (1) Add the two 4-bit BCD digits as binary numbers. (2) If the 4-bit sum exceeds 1001 (9) or a carry is generated, the result is invalid BCD. (3) Add the correction factor 0110 (6) to that digit; the carry propagated to the next digit represents the tens digit.
Correction: 1100 + 0110 = 0001 0010 → BCD digits 0001 (1) and 0010 (2) = decimal 12. Correct, since 5 + 7 = 12.
